intro: Someone left minus-eighty open overnight, and by morning the cold room in Freezer B smelled of warm plastic and thawing glycerol: half the tubes were dead, while the survivors had begun talking in thin, pipette-corked voices. The postdocs have stopped trying to silence them and instead made Mara the archivist, because she files every answer sheet by the big heading at its top, the way the old card catalogues in the corridor stand in strict title order. When a sheet misbehaves she does not flip to the middle or the end; she walks the row from the first heading onward and lets each sheet give up a single letter, calm and unhurried, as if the library itself were reading the damaged collection back to health. The ruined half lies in a bucket for the autoclave; the talking half waits in a line, already sorted, already quiet enough to be heard one letter at a time.
echo: A few of the mice in cage four are two animals at once, and perfectly happy about it.

puzzles.title: Crossover Event
puzzles.flavor: Some buttons are more worn than others.
hints: Old phone multi-tap: the digit is the key, and how many times it repeats picks the letter.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with P.

puzzles.title: Gel Electrophoresis
puzzles.flavor: Cross off everything you recognise. What nobody claims is what you came for.

blocks.text: Hidden in the grid: 8 words to do with the sequencing lab (lengths 6, 6, 7, 7, 7, 7, 8, 8), running in any direction.

hints: Find every hidden word (any of 8 directions). The unused letters, read left-to-right, top-to-bottom, spell the answer.
The hidden words are: EMBRYO, ENZYME, GUANINE, HELICASE, MITOSIS, PEPTIDE, PLASMID, TELOMERE.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with P.

puzzles.title: Central Dogma
puzzles.flavor: The labels in the sequencing lab have faded. Each one lost exactly one letter.
hints: Each theme word is missing one letter. The missing letters, in order, spell the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

puzzles.title: Primer Dimer
puzzles.flavor: Somebody shook the sentence and all the letters fell to the bottom of their columns.
hints: A drop quote: each column's letters (shown alphabetised above it) drop into that column of the grid below. Black squares are spaces; words can wrap between rows. The sentence tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with B.

puzzles.title: Knockout
puzzles.flavor: The chemist in the sequencing lab spelled the word out with the periodic table, one or two letters at a time.
hints: Each number is an atomic number. Write down each element's chemical symbol and read the symbols together as one word.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with P.

puzzles.title: Backup Copy
puzzles.flavor: A familiar grid, an unfamiliar alphabet.
hints: Sudoku using the letters shown instead of digits (each row, column and box uses each letter once). Read the numbered squares in order.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

puzzles.title: Reading Frame
puzzles.flavor: Run up the halyard at dawn and left there: a string of bunting that isn't meant for decoration.
hints: International maritime signal flags, one letter each.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

meta.title: Meta: Cold Storage, Freezer B
meta.flavor: File everything the way an archivist would, by its heading. Then walk down the drawer.
hints: Order the puzzles alphabetically by title; take the k-th letter of the k-th answer.
To check you're on track: the final answer begins with C.
